injuries.description: Substantial facial scarring / permanent cosmetic disability / cosmetic deformity
source: Whilst the wounds healed in due course, the Plaintiff suffered substantial facial scarring and on the 22nd January 1985 she consulted a plastic surgeon Dr. Otto Y.T. Au.

"Right face - Two linear scars as follows : (a) An oblique vertical scar extending from right temporal side-burn to the right cheek measures 9 cm in length, 3 mm wide and showed moderate hypertrophic in nature. (b)Horizontal scar above the anterior portion of the mandible measures 3 cm in length 2 mm wide. Left face - A long curved linear scar extending from left temporal side-burn downward and forward to the masalabial area for a distance of 10 cm, it bifid upward at the anterior end for a distance of 4 cm to the nasalabial area, most of the scar is elevated and its width is 4 mm in diameter. Chin - An oblique scar is formed at the left side of her chin. it measures 4 cm, its width is 2 mm."

In April 1986 the Plaintiff was examined by another plastic surgeon Dr. Ian H. Nicholson whose report was tendered in evidence. I do not propose to quote from the same in detail but will move straight to his prognosis. He considered that the Plaintiff has a permanent cosmetic disability and that whilst the scars would improve a little over the next year or so they would not improve to any significant extent. He added that further plastic surgery cannot lessen her degree of cosmetic disability.

Dr. Tan briefly reviewed the Plaintiff's case history, stated that the Plaintiff was suffering from a post-traumatic stress disorder and, for what it is worth, noted that the Plaintiff's degree of disability was assessed "by our psychiatric Medical Board on 12th April 1985 in the region of 20%".

"(1) Port -Traumatic Stress Disorder : as shown by impairment of sleep fear of situations reminiscent of the incident and recurrent dreams of events related to it. This psychiatric disorder is a psychological reaction to acute traumatic experiences. It is severe in degree. She also has severe anxiety, depressive and psychosomatic (e.g. frequent urination) features associated with the Stress Disorder."

"(2) Personality Disorder (paranoid type) as shown by excessive sensitivity concerning her appearance and her scars in particular an excessive tendency to self-reference in social situations suspiciousness and a sense of subsection and humiliation. The Disorder is impairing her capacity to socialize and work. It is severe in degree."

manifestations.description: Wounds became infected and required drainage of pus and re-suturing
Impairment of sleep, fear of situations reminiscent of the incident and recurrent dreams
Severe anxiety, depressive and psychosomatic features (e.g. frequent urination)
Excessive sensitivity concerning her appearance and her scars, excessive tendency to self-reference in social situations, suspiciousness and a sense of subjection and humiliation
Impairing her capacity to socialize and work
Cosmetic deformity as a result of the scars on her face

treatments_received: Plastic surgery by Dr. Otto Y.T. Au on 15th April 1985
Plastic surgery examination by Dr. Ian H. Nicholson in April 1986
Psychiatric treatment at Psychiatric Centres, mainly in Yaumatei until February 1987
Inpatient treatment at Princess Margaret Hospital (inpatient charges recorded)

losses.description: The Plaintiff suffered substantial facial scarring ... she is in her own eyes if not necessarily those of others, hideously scarred.
She is now a virtual recluse unable even to relax let alone enjoy herself, within the security of her own home.
She is quit unable to live anything approaching a normal life or earn any sort of a living, let alone return to her former job as a hostess.

losses.category: Loss of confidence in going out in the public
